definition: Older Workers Benefit Protection Act (OWBPA) is a 1990 federal law that amended the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA). The Older Workers Benefit Protection Act (OWBPA) protects individuals who are at least 40 years old by clarifying age-discrimination rules for employee benefits and by establishing minimum requirements for a knowing and voluntary waiver of ADEA rights. OWBPA does not require an employer to offer severance pay. For employee benefits, the ADEA generally permits a bona fide benefit plan to provide different benefits only within statutory offset / Older Workers Benefit Protection Act (OWBPA) Dictionary compilation | 26 September 2026 limits, including an equal-benefit or equal-cost framework. The law also recognizes qualifying voluntary early-retirement incentive plans. Employers may not use a benefit plan to require involuntary retirement because of age, and separate provisions restrict age-based cessation or reduction of pension accruals or account allocations. These rules appear principally in 29 U.S.C. § 623. OWBPA is especially important when an employer asks an employee to release age-discrimination claims in exchange for severance or another benefit. Under 29 U.S.C. § 626(f), a valid waiver ordinarily must be in writing and understandable; specifically refer to ADEA rights; exclude claims arising after execution; provide consideration beyond anything to which the employee already is entitled; and advise the employee in writing to consult an attorney. The employee generally must receive at least 21 days to consider an individual agreement and at least seven days after signing to revoke the agreement. If the waiver is requested in connection with an exit-incentive or other employment-termination program offered to a group or class of employees, the consideration period generally is at least 45 days.
